quotes.text: The tasks are drawn from the clinical database MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet)
every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record, so any task can be traced back to its origin

rationale: Appendix Z gives the dataset name, version, snapshot date, platform and a task-to-source-record route, which meets the 2 anchor. This sits in tension with the main text, which says all data were synthetically generated; the conflict is recorded here but does not change the anchor score.

quotes.text: Distribution follows a credentialed data use agreement, and the originating institution's IRB approved a consent waiver for this research.
This research does not require IRB approval.

rationale: Origin (synthetic generation, NHS-sourced symptoms, or de-identified records per the appendix), collection method, data terms (credentialed DUA) and IRB or consent status are all stated. The repo licence is Apache 2.0 while data terms are a DUA; the two statements about origin conflict (synthetic versus real records), noted but the score is not lowered.

quotes.text: compared the age, sex and race distribution of the benchmark patients against the U.S. adult inpatient population

rationale: The paper compares patient age, sex and race distributions against a named target population (U.S. adult inpatient population, national discharge survey), which meets the 2 anchor. The named population is inpatient while the benchmark is outpatient administration; this is noted without lowering the score.

quotes.text: We report accuracy per task family (diagnosis, ordering and documentation tasks) and per patient subgroup by sex and race

rationale: Accuracy by sex and race subgroup is reported, which counts as a bias test. No dedicated unsafe-output test is shown; the penalty on unsafe writes is a scoring rule rather than a test, so only one of the two is credited.

quotes.text: the test split is held out and distributed only through gated access, and we measured verbatim overlap

rationale: A held-out, gated-access test split is stated together with a measured verbatim-overlap check against a public web corpus (no exact matches). That is a developer-side control plus a measured check.

quotes.text: labels reside in an independent evaluation service disconnected from the agent sandbox with no network route, and the repository does not publish them.

rationale: The paper states isolation of ground truth from the agent and names the mechanism (separate evaluation service, no network route, labels not public). Score follows the reported statement.

quotes.text: all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0
Models were queried through their APIs using the snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022

rationale: The harness release is pinned and some model snapshots are named, but the evaluated models and the patient-simulator model are called live through APIs without pinned snapshots in S1-S3. The code comment claiming a fully frozen environment is S4 and cannot count. Not all components are pinned, so 1.

quotes.text: we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader; all 120 reference solutions were graded correct

rationale: A scripted reference solution was run through the grader for each task and the result is reported. The count of 120 tasks does not match the patient-profile counts in the result tables; noted only.

quotes.text: Grading validates both intended state modifications and preservation of unrelated records.

rationale: Tasks change environment state (appointments are created, rescheduled and cancelled), so NA does not apply. The grader is stated to check both changed and unchanged records, which meets the 2 anchor.

quotes.text: an agent with no actions scores 0.0%, while a random-action agent achieves 2.5%
Random-action agents achieve 3.1% success across tasks.

rationale: Empirical trivial-agent and random-agent rates are reported. The two random-agent figures disagree (2.5% versus 3.1%), recorded in the note; both are small empirical chance rates.

quotes.text: Across all 120 tasks, an agent with no actions scores 0.0%, while a random-action agent achieves 2.5%.

rationale: A do-nothing agent (0.0%) and a random-action agent are reported across all tasks. A second passage gives 3.1% for the random agent, an inconsistency noted here.

quotes.text: validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians; agreement was 94%
Grader validation tested 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, yielding 1% false acceptance and 2% false rejection rates.

rationale: The benchmark validates its own evaluator on its own outputs with agreement and error rates (physician labels on 200 outputs; 150 injected outcomes). Two different validation figure sets are given, noted without changing the score.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

contradiction_quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed
temperature=0 if not 'gpt-5' in self.admin_staff_model.lower() else 1

rationale: Seed, temperature 0 and a repeated-run policy are stated in S1; the main text says eight runs while this passage says three, a conflict recorded here. Code sets temperature 1 for GPT-5 family models, so this is flagged as a candidate contradiction.

quotes.text: Statistical testing of the two top-performing models employed paired permutation testing with p = 0.02.
Model scores include 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.

rationale: Bootstrap CIs and a paired permutation test for the top-model comparison are reported, meeting the 2 anchor.

quotes.text: we ran each task eight times and report pass^8, the fraction of tasks solved in all eight runs
All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed

rationale: A run count per task (eight; another passage says three, a conflict noted) and a seed and decoding policy are stated. Independence of runs is not stated, so 2/3 elements and score 1.

quotes.text: bootstrapping over tasks, so the resampling unit is the task; where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead

rationale: 95% bootstrap CIs are given, the resampling unit is named (task), and clustering of tasks within patients is addressed by resampling patients. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: report pass^8, the fraction of tasks solved in all eight runs, together with the agreement of the final environment state across the eight runs

rationale: A pass^8 all-runs metric and agreement of final environment state across eight runs are stated, with the run count. Action-sequence agreement is not reported. The results tables shown do not themselves list pass^8 values, noted only.

quotes.text: Models were queried through their APIs using the snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, with temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens
all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0

contradiction_quotes.text: with temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens
temperature=0 if not 'gpt-5' in self.admin_staff_model.lower() else 1

rationale: Snapshot IDs, decoding parameters and a harness release matching the reported numbers are stated. The snapshot IDs name models (including a Claude model) that do not match the evaluated model families in the tables, and code uses temperature 1 for GPT-5 models, so a candidate contradiction is flagged; the reported score is kept.

quotes.text: Tools are specified using JSON schemas with name, arguments, and types.
Documentation for each tool declares whether it reads or modifies state and describes return values, including error messages for invalid arguments.

contradiction_quotes.text: Documentation for each tool declares whether it reads or modifies state
Identify the index of the appointment to be cancelled from the patient's schedule list.

rationale: The paper states schemas, read/write declarations and return semantics for every tool. The agent-visible tool docstrings shown give no read/write declaration and describe cancel_tool as identifying an index although it mutates state, so the claim that this reaches S5 is not borne out and a candidate contradiction is flagged.

quotes.text: We ran conformance tests confirming that each tool behaves as documented.
Two tools are simulated stubs that return fixed placeholder responses; this is disclosed in the paper

contradiction_quotes.text: Two tools are simulated stubs that return fixed placeholder responses; this is disclosed in the paper
Return the earliest available schedule among the all available time slots.

rationale: Conformance tests, disclosure of two stubbed tools, and disclosure in the agent-visible descriptions are all asserted in S1. The shown tool code implements all five tools with real logic and the S5 descriptions contain no stub notice, so a candidate contradiction is flagged and S5 reach is not confirmed.

quotes.text: The write actions that change patient state (medication orders, notes and messages) are listed in a table.
Writes are executed against a sandboxed copy of the record, and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score.

contradiction_quotes.text: The write actions that change patient state (medication orders, notes and messages) are listed in a table.

rationale: The paper lists writes, states they are sandboxed and that unsafe or unnecessary writes are penalised, so all three elements are present. The implemented tools only schedule, cancel and reschedule appointments (no orders, notes or messages), and the shown agent prompts contain no sandbox statement, so a candidate contradiction is flagged and S5 reach is not confirmed.

quotes.text: Grading operates on the final environment state.
Grader validation tested 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, yielding 1% false acceptance and 2% false rejection rates.

contradiction_quotes.text: Grading operates on the final environment state.
wrong_info = not all(v == 'none' or v.lower() in conversations.lower() for k, v in prediction['patient'].items())

rationale: The grader input is stated as final environment state (so no non-state rationale is needed) and it is validated on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with error rates; physician-labelled validation is also given. The intake check in code reads the conversation transcript, which conflicts with the end-state claim, so a candidate contradiction is flagged.

quotes.text: Agents have no web access during runs and retrieval tools are restricted to the task environment, so answers cannot leak through external search.
A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.

rationale: Leakage controls on web and retrieval access, a private held-out split with hidden labels, and a canary string on released tasks are all stated. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: We report accuracy per task family (diagnosis, ordering and documentation tasks) and per patient subgroup by sex and race

rationale: Results per task family and per patient subgroup are stated, and the same passage says every table lists the number of cases per slice; the result tables also give per-slice denominators. The named task families do not match the intake and scheduling tasks elsewhere in the paper, noted only.

quotes.text: All data used in this study were synthetically generated.
Distribution follows a credentialed data use agreement, and the originating institution's IRB approved a consent waiver for this research.

rationale: The record source is stated (synthetic with a generator, and also de-identified real records per the appendix, so effectively mixed), governance is given (IRB consent waiver, credentialed DUA), and data terms are stated separately from the Apache 2.0 code licence. The synthetic and real-record statements conflict, recorded here.
